title: Mould and mildew spray
subtitle: A vinegar and tea tree spray for bathroom surfaces
excerpt: Mould and mildew spray is a white vinegar solution with tea tree essential oil, used on bathroom tiles, grout, shower curtains, and windowsill edges where surface mould develops. Sprayed on, left for ten minutes, and wiped away, it removes light surface mould and slows regrowth. Makes 300 ml in a spray bottle; keeps six months at room temperature.
sourceNotes: White vinegar (acetic acid 5%) as a mould remover: Natural Cleaning Solutions by Rachel Ogden (2012). Effective against many common household surface moulds at 5% concentration when left to act for 10 minutes (EPA antimicrobial data for acetic acid). Tea tree essential oil antimicrobial properties: Australian Tea Tree Industry Association technical notes (2021). Not effective on porous materials where mould has penetrated deeply (e.g. plasterboard) or on bleach-requiring black mould, those cases require professional treatment or bleach.

recipe.batchNotes: Make in larger batches and refill the spray bottle as needed.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The spray is ready to use immediately.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Six months at room temperature. The vinegar is self-preserving. The tea tree essential oil may cause the spray to go cloudy over time, shake before use. Discard if the spray smells fermented or off rather than sharply vinegary.

content.text: Mould and mildew spray is a white vinegar solution with tea tree essential oil, used on bathroom tiles, grout, shower curtains, and windowsill edges where surface mould develops. Spray on, leave ten minutes, and wipe away to remove light surface mould and slow regrowth. Makes 300 ml; keeps six months.
This spray works on non-porous surfaces. It does not remove mould that has penetrated deeply into grout, plasterboard, or silicone, those cases need physical removal or a bleach-based product.

items.prepNote: distilled white vinegar at 5% acetic acid concentration; the main active ingredient
dilutes the vinegar slightly to reduce the sharp smell on application
~0.3% of total volume; adds antimicrobial properties and a fresher scent over straight vinegar

content.text: Combine the vinegar, water, and tea tree essential oil in the spray bottle. Seal and shake well. The tea tree oil does not fully dissolve in water, shake before each use.

Shake the bottle, then spray directly onto the affected surface. Leave for ten minutes, do not wipe immediately. The acid needs contact time to work on the mould. Wipe with a damp cloth, then rinse with water. For heavy mould on grout lines, apply and leave for 30 minutes before scrubbing with a stiff brush. Do not use on natural stone (marble, travertine, limestone), vinegar etches stone surfaces.

After cleaning, spray the cleaned surface lightly and leave without rinsing to slow regrowth. The main factor in mould return is humidity, ventilate the bathroom after showers and fix any leaks that keep surfaces perpetually damp.
Six months at room temperature. Shake before each use.
